items.question: Can an abstract class have a constructor?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. An abstract class can have a constructor, just like a normal class. The constructor can be declared inside the abstract class even though an object of that abstract class cannot be created directly.

items.question: Can an object of an abstract class be created directly?
items.answer: Answer: No. Java does not allow direct instantiation of an abstract class. Attempting to create an object of an abstract class results in a compilation error.

items.question: If an abstract class has a constructor, how is that constructor executed?
items.answer: Answer: The constructor of an abstract class is executed indirectly when an object of a concrete child class is created. The child constructor invokes the parent constructor through super().

items.question: How does a child class invoke the constructor of an abstract parent class?
items.answer: Answer: When a child-class object is created, the child constructor calls the abstract parent-class constructor using super(). The parent constructor executes as part of the child object's initialization.

items.question: Can an abstract class contain static variables?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. An abstract class can contain static variables. Since a static variable belongs to the class, it can be accessed using the abstract class name without creating an object.

items.question: How can a static variable declared in an abstract class be accessed?
items.answer: Answer: It can be accessed using the class name and dot operator, such as Demo.count. An object of the abstract class is not required to access a static member.

items.question: Can an abstract class contain static methods?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. An abstract class can contain static methods, and they can be called using the abstract class name.

items.question: Can an abstract class contain instance variables?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. An abstract class can contain instance variables. These variables are part of the state of objects created from its concrete child classes.

items.question: Can an abstract class contain an instance initialization block?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. An abstract class can contain an instance initialization block. It is executed as part of initializing a child-class object.

items.question: When is an instance initialization block executed?
items.answer: Answer: An instance initialization block executes after object creation begins and before the constructor body executes.

items.question: Can an abstract class contain instance methods and constructors?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. An abstract class can contain instance methods and constructors, in addition to static members and initialization blocks.

items.question: Which members can be declared inside an abstract class?
items.answer: Answer: An abstract class can contain static variables, static methods, instance variables, instance methods, static initialization blocks, instance initialization blocks, constructors, concrete methods, and abstract methods.

items.question: What is the main restriction of an abstract class?
items.answer: Answer: The key restriction is that an object of the abstract class cannot be created directly. Other members that can be declared in a normal class can also be declared in an abstract class.

items.question: Can an abstract class exist without any abstract methods?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. Java allows a class to be declared abstract even when it does not contain any abstract methods. This can be useful when direct object creation must be prevented.

items.question: Is a class required to be abstract if it contains an abstract method?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. If a class contains an abstract method, the class itself must be declared abstract.

items.question: Is declaring a class abstract compulsory when it has no abstract methods?
items.answer: Answer: No. Java does not force a class without abstract methods to be abstract. It can still be declared abstract when the design requires preventing direct object creation.

items.question: What is the difference between an abstract method and a concrete method?
items.answer: Answer: An abstract method is declared without a method body, while a concrete method has an implementation body.

items.question: What is impure abstraction?
items.answer: Answer: Impure abstraction is an arrangement in which an abstract class contains both abstract methods and concrete methods.

items.question: What is pure abstraction?
items.answer: Answer: Pure abstraction is an arrangement in which the abstraction type contains only abstract methods and no concrete method implementations.

items.question: How can pure abstraction be represented using an abstract class?
items.answer: Answer: A class can be declared abstract and contain only abstract methods. This gives pure abstraction, although an interface is the dedicated construct used for this purpose in the explanation.

items.question: Why is an interface used for pure abstraction?
items.answer: Answer: An interface is used when pure abstraction is required. The interface defines the methods, and implementing classes provide their method bodies.

items.question: Why are interfaces abstract by nature?
items.answer: Answer: An interface is abstract by nature, so it cannot be instantiated directly. Its methods, as presented in this lesson, specify behavior that an implementing class must provide.

items.question: Can an object of an interface be created directly?
items.answer: Answer: No. An interface cannot be instantiated directly because it is abstract. An object of a concrete class that implements the interface must be created instead.

items.question: What is the purpose of the implements keyword in Java?
items.answer: Answer: The implements keyword is used when a class agrees to implement an interface. The class provides method bodies for the abstract methods declared by that interface.

items.question: What is an implementing class?
items.answer: Answer: An implementing class is a class that uses the implements keyword to implement an interface and provide implementations for its abstract methods.

items.question: Why must an implementing class provide method bodies for interface methods?
items.answer: Answer: The interface declares the required methods without providing their implementations in this example. The implementing class must provide the method bodies so that its objects can be created and used.

items.question: What happens if a class implements an interface but does not implement all its abstract methods?
items.answer: Answer: The class must remain abstract if it does not provide implementations for all inherited abstract methods. A concrete class must implement the required abstract methods.

items.question: Can multiple classes implement the same interface?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. Multiple classes can implement the same interface. Each implementing class can provide its own implementation of the interface methods.

items.question: Can two classes provide different implementations of the same interface method?
items.answer: Answer: Yes. Two implementing classes can provide different method bodies for the same interface method. Each class implements the required behavior according to its own needs.

items.question: What is the difference between extends and implements in the context of this lesson?
items.answer: Answer: The extends keyword is used when one class inherits from another class. The implements keyword is used when a class implements an interface and provides implementations for its abstract methods.
